# Spaces on MORK

> Put a space's atoms in MORK's Rust trie instead of the engine's own store.
> You reach it by NAME: a space called `&mork` is one. This file is how to USE
> the seat; the repository root's llms.txt covers everything else.

## Build

```sh
sh extensions/mork/build.sh
```

Needs `cargo`. Without the artefacts the seat does not load, and a program that
needs it is told so by name rather than failing at the call:

```metta
!(require-extension! mork)
```

## Using it

Any space whose name begins `&mork` is stored in MORK:

```metta
!(add-atom &mork (parent alice bob))
!(match &mork (parent $x bob) $x)
```

The three builtins the seat adds:

| builtin | what it does |
|---|---|
| `(mork-add-atoms &mork ...)` | add many atoms in ONE crossing |
| `(mork-flush &mork)` | push buffered writes through |
| `(mm2-exec &mork ...)` | run MM2 steps inside MORK itself |

`lib_mm2` is the MeTTa-level surface over those, five operators over `&mork`:

```metta
!(import! &self (library lib_mm2))
```

## When it is worth it

Measured at 500, 2000 and 8000 atoms against a native space:

| | 500 | 2000 | 8000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| batch add against one add per atom | 0.34x | 0.33x | 0.33x |
| writing, against a native space | 2.31x | 2.26x | 2.20x |
| query with the FIRST argument bound | 10.31x | 10.34x | 10.32x |
| query with the LAST argument bound | 46.62x | 133.83x | 611.51x |

Read that as the store's shape. MORK holds an atom as a PATH, so a bound first
argument is a prefix it descends to in constant time, and a bound last argument
is a constraint it can only check after walking. Use the batch door, which is
worth three of the per-atom door at every size, and write queries that bind
early arguments.

## Where to read next

- `extensions/mork/README.md` explains the seat and its needs.
- `lib/lib_mm2/lib_mm2.metta` is the operator surface, and its first line is
  the `require-extension!` above.
